conditional_transfer_preconditions: Source and destination refer to valid initialized list storage, with counts consistent with the accessible source and destination record ranges.
Index arithmetic, including count * 0x360 + 8, does not overflow and every selected memory access is valid.
Called helpers return normally and obey the ordinary ABI, including preservation of nonvolatile registers used by the caller.

Counts and relevant source bytes stay stable across intervening reads and calls, apart from the destination-count changes described here. The code reloads counts after helpers; an initial-count snapshot is not generally guaranteed.
Source/destination overlap, helper aliases and callbacks do not change unread source bytes, list headers or object lifetime. Arbitrary overlap-safe snapshot semantics are not proved.

count_widths.list_copy_helper: QWORD (64-bit) loads/stores of the container header at base.
count_widths.retained_DFE7D0_consumer: DWORD (32-bit) loads at DFF516 and DFF90C.

paths.same_pointer: Entry equality branch goes to 6B5F95; the decoded epilogue returns destination, with no explicit container writes or helper calls on that path.
paths.existing_records: Unsigned-minimum loop passes destination+8+i*0x360 and source+8+i*0x360 to 6B9A50 at 6B5BF7. Counts are reloaded after the opaque call. Existing-record field behavior remains unproved here.
paths.append: When destination count is below source count, current destination count supplies i. The code constructs the new record at destination+8+i*0x360 from the corresponding source address, increments the 64-bit destination count and repeats while below source count.
paths.shrink: When destination count exceeds source count, the code decrements it and invokes cleanup helpers for removed records. Complete destructor and alias effects remain open.
